name: jarvis-app
description: Kairos — a self-hosted AI workspace and agent harness.
//build.files: build.files uses *.js rather than naming main.js and preload.js individually. It is an ALLOWLIST, so a new main-process module is silently omitted from the package: electron/browser.js was, and 1.9.0 shipped an app whose main process died on require() before starting the backend, so it never opened at all. The glob means the next module added here is packaged automatically. Verify with scripts/verify-packaged-app.cjs, which checks main.js's relative requires against the real asar and then launches the packaged app. This note lives at the top level because electron-builder rejects unknown keys inside build.
//build.extraResources: The backend **/* filter includes tabs/** exactly as it includes routes/**. Prebuilt tabs must ship even while disabled; data/** remains excluded so user tabs stay in the user's data folder. scripts/verify-packaged-app.cjs checks the actual School files in the packaged backend. `!.git` and `!.venv` sit beside `!.git/**` and `!.venv/**` because a git worktree's .git is a FILE (it held the build path in 2.3.0-beta.1) and a worktree's .venv can be a junction (2.2.1's first installer packed the whole dev venv through one); the /** forms match only a folder's contents. The Windows installer also carries Microsoft's vc_redist.x64.exe (electron/redist, fetched and pinned by scripts/build_runtime.py, run by vcredist.nsh only when missing); it is not part of the app's files.
//productName: Top-level (not just under build) on purpose: Electron's app.getName() prefers productName over name, and that name decides app.getPath('userData') — i.e. where every user's data lives. Without this it resolved to %APPDATA%\jarvis-app. Since the Kairos rename (2.0.0) electron/instance.js pins the ordinary app's userData to %APPDATA%\JARVIS, so productName no longer decides where data lives; never remove that pin, or existing installs' data is silently orphaned.
//electronFuses: Kairos Browser U0 (vault: Kairos Browser - Phase 1). Electron stores cookies in plain text unless EnableCookieEncryption is flipped; Phase 0 confirmed that on disk. electron-builder flips it right before signing, after afterPack.js, so resetAdHocDarwinSignature re-signs the macOS ad-hoc signature the flip breaks. Cookies saved before the flip are rewritten once by browser-engine.js. The electron dependency is castlabs' ECS build (Widevine for DRM video), from GitHub rather than npm. build.electronDist packages that installed, checksum-verified binary: electron-builder would otherwise fetch its own copy from electron/electron's releases, where castlabs' version does not exist (a 404 on the first build).
author: David Darr
